- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., drops below 0.2) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per 2-day sentiment decline.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak but price history shows strong upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 5-day avg > 75% of 30d avg.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment turns sharply negative.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.4–0.6) and price is trending sideways, model overfits to recent volatility; use 30d moving average as baseline, not 30d forecast.
